clue.text: Home match not in series

parts.note: at home means in
to match something is to parallel it

explanation.surface: A home fixture that is not part of a league series of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'series' is the electrician's word here: components are wired either in series or side by side, one beside another.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrical wiring, components not connected in series are connected side by side across the same supply.

clue.text: Before noon, painter ran out of tint for Cupid

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: the painter has run out of the word tint, so it is taken away from his name

parts.note: Tintoretto, the Venetian Renaissance painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the morning an artist ran short of colour while painting Cupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran out of' removes TINT from TINTORETTO, leaving ORETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a small winged cherub of love in Italian art, a little Cupid figure.

clue.text: Invest £1000 in a promising merchantman

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so this money is wrapped up inside the following words
says where the thousand pounds is put: within the next words

parts.note: a promising future is a rosy one
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Advice to put a thousand pounds into a trading ship with good prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: An argosy is a large old merchant ship, and a merchantman is a trading vessel.

clue.text: TV, one of many used by painter

definitions.meaning: the box or telly, television being called the ... in American slang

definitions.text: one of many used by painter
definitions.meaning: oil paints come in small squeezable containers

explanation.surface: Television, and one of a painter's many paint containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is informally the box; painters keep colours in squeezable containers of this name.

clue.text: Head Office ploy to bag golf record creates mess

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a sack, so the ploy holds the next pieces

parts.note: a dodge is a crafty ploy
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A management scheme at headquarters to hide a golf score causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bag' puts the golf and record letters inside the ploy, straight after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hodgepodge is a jumbled mixture, a confused muddle of things.

clue.text: Russian writer set to keep pressure on northeast

indicators.note: the set holds what follows within it

parts.note: a TV set
to urge is to press, so urge means pressure
NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: A Russian author is ready to keep pushing towards the northeast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like 'ready'; it is a television set, which 'to keep' wraps around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the nineteenth-century Russian novelist of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Regime controller cut out missing painter

indicators.note: the controller is missing the next words' letters, so they are taken away

parts.note: a dietitian controls a person's diet, or regime
to die is to cut out shapes, as a die-cutter does

explanation.surface: A dictator's overseer has been removed, leaving a painter unaccounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance artist of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Exhibit Holbeins and new Goyas at the front

indicators.note: only the front letter of each of these words is wanted

explanation.surface: A gallery's instruction to show the Holbeins and new Goyas in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang pictures is to exhibit them on a gallery wall.

clue.text: The best thing on our menu? Flounders

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle about clumsily, so the words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A waiter recommends the flounder as the menu's best dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounders' looks like the fish being served; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Numero uno, Italian for number one, is the top person or thing.

clue.text: New York city swamped by pharmaceuticals

indicators.note: the city is engulfed by the long word, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A New York town is overrun by the drugs industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Utica is a city in upstate New York State, on the Mohawk River.

clue.text: A top-class part pouches European gold disk

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: to pouch is to put in a pouch, so the part holds the next letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A star performer's role pockets a European gold disc award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold disk' suggests a record award; it is the golden circle round a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureole is a halo, the golden circle of light painted around a holy figure.

clue.text: Carriage twice tours north doing odd jobs

indicators.note: the doubled carriage goes round the next letter, enclosing it
the carriage word is written two times over

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled carriage

explanation.surface: A carriage making two trips around the north while running errands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' puts N inside GIGGIG, before the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigging is taking short-term freelance work, a string of one-off paid tasks.

clue.text: Restless colonists close to colony

parts.note: ants live in colonies, so they are colonists

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Settlers grow uneasy near their settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for fidgety and impatient, as if ants were crawling on you.

clue.text: Old parish priest, one notes, regularly makes enemies

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: An elderly vicar notices that some people make a habit of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents are adversaries, those set against you in a contest.

clue.text: Former golf tournament, such as 7 and 16

definitions.note: plural: Titian and Leonardo are two examples

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
the Masters is the annual golf major at Augusta

explanation.surface: A golf event of the past, such as two famous painters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at two other answers, Titian (7) and Leonardo da Vinci (16).
explanation.definitionFit: Great European painters before about 1800, such as Titian and Leonardo, are called by this name.

clue.text: Paintings fill up boring gaps in walls

indicators.note: boring into something means drilling inside it

parts.note: stiles are steps or openings for crossing country walls

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Pictures used to plug dull holes in walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' writes 'fill' bottom to top as LLIF, since this is a down entry; 'boring' drills it into the stiles after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Still lifes are pictures of arranged objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: He could give advice on oil and colour ultimately

indicators.note: the letters could produce, or give rise to, another arrangement
the ultimate, final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An artist who might advise on oil paint and colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could give' mixes ADVICE ON OIL AND with R, the last letter of 'colour'. The whole clue also describes the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo, the Renaissance genius, is a man, so 'he' stands for him in the surface.

clue.text: Remove Pollock work for one

definitions.meaning: to take something out or extract it

explanation.surface: Take away a Jackson Pollock painting, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to take out; Pollock's drip paintings are non-representational art.

clue.text: Plants one's managed to gather, so heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means everything is written upwards
the two pieces gather round the next word, holding it between them

parts.note: one is I, and one's is I'S, or IS
ran a business means managed it
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A gardener has managed to collect plants and is now travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to gather' puts the Latin word between the other two pieces, giving ISSICRAN; 'heading north' turns that upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodils and their relatives, bulbs flowering in spring.

clue.text: Painting Loch Ness with monster's eye in it

indicators.note: the next letter goes into the pieces just built

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake
and means with, together
a ness is a headland, so a cape
the eye, or middle, of the word monster is its central letter S

explanation.surface: A picture of Loch Ness featuring the monster's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ness' is not the loch but a headland, CAPE. The S, the middle letter of 'monster', goes inside before CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of countryside or natural scenery.

clue.text: Silly person, old one, needing treatment

indicators.note: the words must be treated, or worked on, to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A fool, an elderly person, in need of medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is an informal name for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Beginner left part of Austria

parts.note: a tyro is a novice or beginner

explanation.surface: A novice has departed from an Austrian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrol is the alpine state of western Austria around Innsbruck.

clue.text: Gift storybooks

parts.note: story gives tale, and the books are NT, the New Testament books of the Bible
the books part of the word is NT, the New Testament books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A present of storybooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'storybooks' splits in two, giving a story and then the New Testament's abbreviation for a collection of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural ability or flair.

clue.text: Old horse reverses to and fro unsteadily, due to this?

definitions.text: Old horse reverses to and fro unsteadily, due to this?

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, also called horse

indicators.note: moving unsteadily, the letters wobble into a new order
the next word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An aged horse staggers back and forth, perhaps because of a foot disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' turns FRO into OFR; 'reverses' turns TO into OT. Read whole, the clue suggests why a horse might stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoof rot is a bacterial foot disease of livestock that can leave an animal lame and unsteady.

clue.text: Prince Harry's portrait painter

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Prince Henry, known as Harry
the possessive ending, taken as written

explanation.surface: The artist who painted Prince Harry's likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry IV plays call young Henry (Harry) Prince Hal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was the Dutch Golden Age master of lively portraits such as The Laughing Cavalier.

clue.text: Call trendy current painter

parts.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them
in means fashionable
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Phone a fashionable contemporary artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day'; it is the symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Bellini was a leading Venetian Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Scrap paper behind folio

parts.note: bum is British slang for the behind, the bottom

explanation.surface: Waste sheets placed after a book's page.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork, from bum-fodder, toilet paper.

clue.text: Ring back about newspaper plant

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the next letter
the word is written backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the Independent's sister paper, the i

explanation.surface: Phone back regarding a newspaper story about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC, which goes 'about' I after its first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white flower clusters.

clue.text: Reflect on revealing wear on small church

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a miniskirt, or mini, shows a lot of leg
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Musing over skimpy clothes worn at a little chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to think back over the past, recalling memories.
